name: quilm
author: everyday-object semantics (lateral)
description: Matchstick moves on a seven-segment display. Clue: 'X/N', X a 3..6 digit number, N in 1..4. Solution: a number Y of the same length that X becomes when exactly N segments are switched OFF and exactly N are switched ON over the whole display -- 'move exactly N matchsticks and read the new number'. With masks 0..9 = 63,6,91,79,102,109,125,7,127,111 (bits a..g): sum of popcount(Y_i & ~X_i) == N and sum of popcount(X_i & ~Y_i) == N. The two counts being equal means Y lights exactly as many segments as X in total -- sticks are moved, not added. One-stick single-digit moves: 0<->9, 0<->6, 6<->9, 2<->3, 3<->5, 5<->9, 8->0/6/9 (removes one), 1->7 / 3->9 / 6->8 / 9->8 / 0->8 (adds one), so a lone add must be paid for by a removal elsewhere in the number. Y=X scores 0 (nothing moved). GENERATOR CONSTRAINT, NOT A SCORING CLAUSE: a clue is only emitted when no rearrangement of X's own digits is a valid answer. Permuting X preserves its segment total for free, so otherwise 'clue reversed' / 'clue sorted' / a random permutation score ~11% with no insight at all and hand out labelled equations. v2 blocked those in the scorer instead; both Opus players hit the rejection, could not explain it, and rightly called it undiscoverable, so it now lives in generate(), where it costs the player nothing: every answer satisfying the stated rule scores 1. k is re-weighted because the survival rate falls with length (~50% at k=3, ~6% at k=6). HISTORY: v1 (challenges/lab/quilm.v1.json, 'total segments added = N') was cracked by both Opus players in rounds 4 and 6 using fixed-answer identification scans -- a scalar rule 'property(answer) == clue' is an oracle for that property. v2 (quilm.v2.json) made validity relative to the clue, which killed the scan, and was cracked FASTER, in rounds 3 and 5: 'move k matchsticks on a seven-segment display' is a famous puzzle genre, so once a few accepted single-digit edits (9->0, 2->3, 3->2) are visible the model pattern-matches the whole rule. Diagnosis and a v3 sketch are in challenges/lab/NOTES_everyday.md. CLASSIFICATION: too easy for Opus-level centaurs (four crackers out of four, none needing more than 3 demos in v2); a good class for kid-level play. PRIVATE: never shown to players.
